record.context_brief: Largest isospectral families at fixed dimension and volume
record.original_question: Fix a dimension d and a volume x. What is the largest possible cardinality of a family of spherical space forms of dimension d and volume x that are pairwise isospectral and pairwise non-isometric?

evidence.quote: Problem 8.1. Fix a dimension d. What is the maximal cardinality of an isospectral set of spherical space forms of volume x and dimension d?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A spherical space form of dimension $d$ is a compact Riemannian manifold of the form $S^d/\Gamma$, where $S^d$ is the round unit $d$-sphere and $\Gamma \subset O(d+1)$ is a finite subgroup acting freely by isometries; its volume is $\mathrm{vol}(S^d)/|\Gamma|$. Two such manifolds are isospectral if the spectra of their Laplace–Beltrami operators (with multiplicities) coincide, and isometric if there is a Riemannian isometry between them.

Fix an integer $d \ge 2$ and a positive real number $x$. Determine
$$N(d,x) \;=\; \sup\bigl\{\,|\mathcal F| \,:\, \mathcal F \text{ is a family of spherical space forms of dimension } d \text{ and volume } x,$$
$$\text{which are pairwise isospectral and pairwise non-isometric}\bigr\}.$$
What is the largest possible cardinality $N(d,x)$, as a function of $d$ and $x$?
artifact.category_tag: spectral geometry of spherical space forms
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of determining the maximal cardinality of an isospectral, pairwise non-isometric family of spherical space forms of fixed dimension and volume appears to be open. Recent work (e.g., a 2024 preprint on "Isospectral spherical space forms and orbifolds of highest volume") addresses related extremal questions about the highest volume at which isospectral pairs occur, and constructs infinite families of pairwise eigenvalue-equivalent lens spaces in odd dimensions, but no general formula for the maximal cardinality at fixed $(d,x)$ is established.

status_evidence.title: Isospectral spherical space forms and orbifolds of highest volume
status_evidence.snippet: Isospectral pairs of spherical space forms of largest volume are realized by lens spaces, at least in low dimensions...
status_evidence.claim: Recent research addresses extremal volumes for isospectral spherical space forms but does not resolve the maximal cardinality question.

status_evidence.title: On spherical space forms which are isospectral but not isometric
status_evidence.snippet: Constructions of isospectral non-isometric spherical space forms.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of isospectral non-isometric pairs is classical, but the supremum of cardinalities remains unsettled.
